text:
kevin: Heads up — multiple customers opened support tickets about 502s and consistent 30s timeouts hitting hosted generation endpoints in eu-west. Started ~09:42 UTC. Sample customer trace: https://livetrace.redwood/trace/abc12345 Request IDs: req_9f1a, req_9f2b

maria (SRE): @oliver can you grab oncall? Any quick pattern (model, region, auth) or is it widespread?

support-bot: New escalation created: ESCL-2026-327. Attached initial logs and customer snippets.

oliver (oncall): I’m on it. Initial look — error spike concentrated in eu-west ingress -> inference-proxy -> runtime path. 502s from proxy with upstream read_timeout. Correlates with rdx-large-q4 route.

jonathan (runtime): I'm seeing large batching latencies and queue time spikes around the same window. Batcher logs show repeated errors: `KVCache stall` and `batcher: failed to flush in flush_deadline`. Not seeing recent model changes.

alice (platform): Could be a combination of a traffic spike + slow kernel hot path. Can we enable fallback to a compatible smaller model for that route while we triage? Propose enabling `fallback:tiered-compat` for eu-west for 15m.

john (support): I'll notify affected customers that we're investigating and may enable a temporary fallback to keep them online. Draft: "We're aware of timeouts/502s in EU — we've applied a temporary fallback while we investigate; will follow up with root cause and ETA."

oliver (oncall): Mitigation applied at 09:05 UTC — enabled fallback to `rdx-medium-q3` for the eu-west route and increased proxy read_timeout from 20s -> 35s as a safety net. Observed error-rate drop: 14% -> 1.6% within ~3 minutes. Rolling stability checks now.

maria (SRE): Good containment. Can you paste the key logs/snippets and the livetrace links for the incident timeline? We need them for the postmortem.

oliver (oncall): Logs/trace: ``HTTP 502 from inference-proxy: upstream read timeout
upstream: runtime-4a3f
trace: https://livetrace.redwood/trace/abc12345
batcher error sample: [2026-03-17T09:42:11Z] batcher: flush_deadline exceeded, queue_length=312``

jonathan (runtime): Action plan: 1) Investigate batcher config and KV cache behavior under this workload (owner: jonathan). 2) Run a controlled replay of the captured traces in a staging cluster to reproduce queueing (owner: oliver + runtime). 3) Evaluate kernel/quantization hot path telemetry around the spike (owner: research/eng-ml).

alice (platform): Platform actions: 1) Add temporary circuit-breaker on rdx-large-q4 route to fail-fast to fallback sooner (owner: alice). 2) Short-term autoscaler tweak to scale more aggressively on queue depth for eu-west (owner: alice).

maria (SRE): Support actions: 1) Support to send formal update to customers (owner: john). 2) Tie ticket ESCL-2026-327 to postmortem and track SLA exposure (owner: kevin).

john (support): I'll send the message and schedule a follow-up call with the top affected accounts.

kevin: I'll update the escalation and ping CSMs. Also flagging this for a 1-hr post-incident review at 12:00 UTC.

oliver (oncall): Current status: fallbacks active, error rates stable ~1.2% last 5m, monitoring for regressions. Planning postmortem once batcher/kv root cause is narrowed down.

maria (SRE): Action items recap (owners):
- Investigate batcher/KV cache + reproduce in staging (jonathan / oliver)
- Implement route circuit-breaker + autoscaler tweak (alice)
- Customer comms + SLA tracking (john / kevin)
- Postmortem write-up + mitigation timeline (maria)

kevin: Thanks everyone — will update ESCL-2026-327 and close the live war room when we have the postmortem links. :thumbsup:
